llm_request: WeDriveAnywhere is a taxi company in a major city. At present their taxis are available at the railway station and at large retail centres. Customers can also book a taxi by phone. Ali, the owner and manager, are investigating the introduction of new technology to make booking and paying for a taxi more efficient and easier for the customer. (a) Explain three ways in which technology could be used to improve booking and payment.
llm_response:
Here are three ways in which technology could be used to improve the booking and payment processes for WeDriveAnywhere:

**1. Development of a Dedicated Mobile Application (Booking Improvement)**
WeDriveAnywhere could introduce a custom smartphone app for iOS and Android devices. Instead of waiting on hold to speak to a dispatcher over the phone, customers could use the app to book a taxi with a single tap. The app could utilize GPS technology to automatically detect the customer's exact location and match them with the nearest available driver at the railway station or retail centre. Furthermore, the app can provide real-time tracking, allowing the customer to see the driver approaching on a map, alongside an accurate Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA). This makes booking highly efficient and removes the communication delays often associated with phone calls.

**2. Contactless and In-App Payment Gateways (Payment Improvement)**
To make paying easier and faster, Ali could integrate cashless payment options. If a customer uses a mobile app, they could securely store their debit/credit card details or link digital wallets (like Apple Pay or Google Pay) to their profile. The fare would be automatically deducted at the end of the journey without the customer having to physically hand over cash or wait for change. Even for walk-up customers at the railway station, Ali could install contactless card terminals in the back of every taxi. This speeds up the drop-off process for the driver and provides a highly secure, frictionless experience for the customer.

**3. Smart Kiosks and Dynamic QR Codes (Booking & Payment Improvement)**
For walk-up customers at the railway station or large retail centres, WeDriveAnywhere could install interactive, self-service smart kiosks. Instead of waiting in a physical line for the next available taxi, a customer could walk up to the screen, input their destination, and book a taxi instantly. Alternatively, WeDriveAnywhere could display dynamic QR codes around these busy hubs. Customers could simply scan the code with their smartphone camera, which would instantly open a web-based booking and payment portal. This allows customers to secure and pay for their ride without needing to download an app or make a phone call, effectively managing high-volume queues during peak times.
